text:
Can you write an email to people who didn't renew their farm share? I run a 30-acre vegetable farm and sell 22-week shares that people pick up every Thursday.

Facts:
- Last year 260 households had a share. 97 didn't renew.
- On July 9 a hailstorm destroyed about half our crops. For the next 6 weeks the boxes had about half the usual amount. We didn't offer refunds or credit, and I sent one short email about it.
- A full share is $540 this year, the same as last year.
- This year we've added a second field on higher ground and put up 2 hail nets over our tomatoes and peppers. That cost $31,000.
- Members can now pause up to 2 weeks and get credit for them.
- Sign-up closes March 15. 52 shares are left.

Under 200 words.

Before I draft this, a few questions. These readers have a grievance: for six weeks they paid full price for half a box, got no credit, and heard about it in one short email. Whether the email wins anyone back depends mostly on how it handles that.

1. **Do you want to apologize, and how far are you willing to go?** Something like "we should have offered credit and told you more" will land very differently from just explaining the storm. I'll write whatever you can honestly stand behind.
2. **Are you offering lapsed members anything?** For example a discount, a free week, or early access. If not, that's fine. I just don't want to invent an offer you don't have.
3. **If a storm hits again, what happens to members' boxes?** Is there now a policy on credit or refunds when the harvest falls short? The new pause option helps, but it doesn't cover a crop loss. This is the question these readers most need answered.
4. **What do the second field and the hail nets actually protect?** The nets cover tomatoes and peppers only. Does the higher field help against hail, or against flooding? I want to describe it accurately without overpromising.
5. **How does the pause credit work?** Is it credit toward that season, a later season, or a refund? How much notice do members have to give?
6. **The basics:** the farm name, who signs, and how people sign up (a link or a reply). Also, has anything else changed that these readers would notice, like the pickup location or time?

1. Yes, I want to say sorry plainly. I only sent one short email because I was working 16-hour days trying to save what was left, but that's not an excuse. We should have done better.
2. No offer for lapsed members.
3. New this year: if weather cuts a box by more than a third, members get a credit for that week. I'll also send a short email to members every Thursday of the season. But I can't promise there won't be any crop loss this year.
4. The nets cover only the tomatoes and peppers, not the greens. For the higher field, I don't know how to say exactly what it protects against beyond it being on higher ground.
5. I don't know the details on how the pause credit works yet.
6. Greenbank Farm, signed by me, Sam Turner. Sign-up is through the link on our website. Pickup is still Thursdays at the farm stand. Nothing else has changed.

Here's the draft. It comes to about 190 words, counting the sign-off and not the subject line.

<final_document>
Subject: We let you down last summer

Hi,

You didn't renew your Greenbank Farm share this year, and I understand why. After the July 9 hailstorm destroyed about half our crops, your boxes held about half the usual amount for six weeks. We didn't offer credit, and I sent one short email. I was working 16-hour days trying to save what was left, but that's not an excuse. I'm sorry. We should have done better.

Here's what's changed:

- If weather cuts a box by more than a third, you get credit for that week.
- I'll email you every Thursday during the season.
- We put up two hail nets over the tomatoes and peppers and added a second field on higher ground, at a cost of $31,000. The nets don't cover the greens, and I can't promise there will be no crop loss this year.
- You can now pause up to two weeks and get credit for them.

A full share is still $540, the same as last year, with pickup Thursdays at the farm stand. Sign-up closes March 15, and 52 shares are left. The link is on our website.

I'd be glad to have you back.

Sam Turner
Greenbank Farm
</invoke>
</final_document>

- **Apology first:** The email apologizes before asking for anything, because these readers already hold last summer against you. The new weather credit is the most direct answer to their complaint, so it comes first in the list.
- **Higher field:** I only said the field is on higher ground. Since you weren't sure what it protects against, the email doesn't claim anything more.
- **Pause credit:** Once you've settled how it works, add a short clause, like "credit toward a later week." Some readers will want to know before they sign up.
- **Sign-up link:** Pasting the actual sign-up link in place of "the link is on our website" would make it easier for people to sign up.
